Commands

Complete reference for CLI commands and TUI key bindings.

TUI

Running mp with no arguments launches a full-screen terminal interface built on ratatui: a mailbox sidebar, the message list, and the headers and body of the selected message. mp -A <account> opens it on that account. The sidebar hides below 40 columns and the right panes below 80.

Like the CLI and the Mac app, the TUI is a client of the local daemon, which syncs every account and pushes new mail to it.

Selectors

Every command that names a message takes a selector, never a file path: mp://<account>/<mailbox>/<key>. For received mail the key is the Message-ID without its angle brackets; for a draft the mailbox is the reserved name drafts and the key is the id: field in the draft's frontmatter, so renaming the file does not change its selector.

The leading segments can be left off: the account falls back to -A/--account or the first account in your config, and the mailbox to --mailbox or the command's own scope. mp send 9f2c1ab30d5e4471 and mp send mp://work/drafts/9f2c1ab30d5e4471 are the same command. A key that matches messages in two mailboxes is reported with both full selectors rather than resolved by guesswork; --mailbox picks one. When one mailbox holds two copies of a message, the refusal lists each with its UID appended, mp://<account>/<mailbox>/<key>/<uid>, and that selector names the one copy. Every command that creates or lists something prints the fully qualified form, which pastes straight into the next command, and mp path <selector> is the one way back to a filesystem path.

A received selector that names its mailbox works even when no sync stored the message, as for a server hit of mp search: show, save, open, export, reply, forward, archive, move, delete and invite fetch it from the server first and say so on stderr. When the store holds the message in another mailbox, the reads, replies and forwards use that copy; archive, move and delete refuse and name its selector, since the Inbox and Sent copies of a message are two messages on the server.

On a terminal, mp new, mp edit, mp reply, mp forward, mp mark-approved and mp mark-draft print ✓ <selector>, mp archive and mp move print the selector they moved the message to under ✓ archived or ✓ moved, and mp save prints ✓ <path> per file. When stdout is a pipe or a file, each prints only the bare selector or path, one per line, so sel=$(mp new note) && mp path "$sel" works as written.

Draft Commands

Command Description
mp <selector> Preview a draft (dry-run)
mp new <name> [-s <name>|--no-signature] Create a new draft from template and print its selector
mp list [--status draft|approved|sent] [--json] List the account's drafts (--json prints them as JSON on stdout)
mp validate [<selector>] Validate one draft, or every draft of the account
mp path <selector> Print the filesystem path of a draft
mp edit <selector> Open a draft in $EDITOR
mp mark-approved <selector> Mark draft as approved
mp mark-draft <selector> Demote approved draft back to draft
mp delete <drafts-selector> [--force] Delete a draft (file + index row); --force is required for an approved draft
mp delete --sent Clear every sent draft of the account
mp send <selector> [-y] Send a single approved email
mp send --invite ... Send a calendar invitation (iMIP REQUEST)
mp send-approved [--all-accounts] [-y] Send every approved draft of the account
mp outbox list [--json] Show queued, retrying, failed and partly delivered submissions (--json prints them as JSON on stdout)
mp outbox retry <id> Send a failed submission again
mp outbox discard <id> Drop a submission and release its bytes
mp reply <selector> [--all] [--mailbox <name>] [-s <name>|--no-signature] Create a reply draft and print its selector
mp forward <selector> [--mailbox <name>] [--as-attachment] [-s <name>|--no-signature] Create a forward draft and print its selector; --as-attachment attaches the original as an .eml (message/rfc822, quoted thread and attachments inside) instead of carrying its attachments, under a body holding only the signature

IMAP Commands

Command Description
mp sync [options] Sync local folders with server
mp watch [options] Watch mailbox for changes (IMAP IDLE)
mp list-mailboxes [--json] List every folder on the server with its sync policy (sync, status-only, ignore) and its role, or why it is ignored (--json prints them as JSON on stdout)
mp archive <selector> [--mailbox <name>] Archive a received email (server + local)
mp move <selector> <mailbox> [--mailbox <name>] Move a received email to another mailbox (server + local), named by role, slug or label (inbox, Junk, archive); an unknown name lists the account's mailboxes, and the mailbox the message is already in is refused
mp delete <selector> [--mailbox <name>] Delete a received email (server + local), or a local draft with a drafts selector
mp search <query> [--json] Search emails on the server with one grammar (fields, has:attachment, dates, OR groups); --local searches the store offline; --json prints the hits as JSON on stdout
mp open <selector> [--mailbox <name>] Open the attachments in the default app; a message whose only parts are inline images opens those
mp save <selector> [--output <dir>] [--mailbox <name>] Save the attachments and the inline images to a directory, fetching the message from the server first when the store lacks it and the selector names its mailbox
mp export <selector> [--output <dir>] [--mailbox <name>] Write the raw message (RFC 822, quoted thread included) to <date>_<subject>.eml in a directory, ready to attach to another mail; a message stored without its raw form (every Graph message) is downloaded from the server

Local Store Commands

Offline reads over what mp sync already brought down. They open no connection: they answer from the per-account store, so they work on a plane and cost nothing. The one exception is mp show of a message the store does not hold, below.

Command Description
mp list-messages [--mailbox <name>] [-n N] [--json] List received messages from the local store (offline; --json prints them as JSON on stdout)
mp show <selector> [--mailbox <name>] [--json] Print one received message (headers, attachments, inline images and body) from the local store, fetching it from the server first when the store lacks it and the selector names its mailbox
mp search --local <query> [--mailbox <name>] [-n N] [--full] [--json] Ranked full-text search over the local store (offline, every synced mailbox at once)
Command Description
--mailbox <name> Mailbox to list (role, slug or sidebar label). Default: every mailbox of the account, grouped
-n, --limit <N> Max messages per mailbox listed (default: 20)
-A, --account <name> Account to read (default: first in config)
--json Emit one JSON object instead of the human layout (mp show: the message; mp list-messages and mp search: the listing, with selectors and ISO 8601 dates)

mp list-messages prints one line per message with its full selector, which pastes straight into mp show, mp reply or mp archive. A mailbox that holds two copies of one message lists each with its UID appended (mp://<account>/<mailbox>/<key>/<uid>), so every line names its own copy; mp search does the same. With no --mailbox it lists every mailbox of the account, grouped, and the limit applies per mailbox so a busy inbox cannot hide the others. The order is the one the TUI's flat list shows (tc switches an account to it).

mp show takes the same selector grammar as every other message command, so the bare Message-ID is enough when it is unambiguous, and an mp://<account>/... selector reads that account's store rather than the default one. A selector that names its mailbox but no message the store holds, such as a sent message mp search found on the server that no sync stored, is fetched from the server into the store first, with a note on stderr; mp save and mp open do the same. A body the store no longer holds (evicted, or never ingested) prints as a note under the headers instead of failing. --json is the parseable form: one object with the envelope, the attachment list and the body as a JSON string. The body's inline images (a signature logo, a pasted screenshot, a phone photo) print under their own Inline images: heading after the attachments, and carry "inline": true in the JSON list.

mp dump-mailbox --json is a different tool with a similar shape: it is the parity oracle, emits newline-delimited envelopes without bodies for every account, and its record shape is pinned. Read mail with these two; diff stores with that one.

Maintenance Commands

Command Description
mp hooks list [--json] List the mail hooks of [[accounts.hooks]] with their cursor and last run (every account unless -A names one)
mp hooks test <hook> <selector> [--json] Check a hook against a stored message: each match criterion's verdict, the authenticated sender among them; runs nothing
mp hooks replay <hook> <selector> Run a hook for a stored message now, in the daemon, behind the same match table; the cursor does not move
mp store gc [--dry-run] [--force] [--all-accounts] Run the retention sweep now: evict cached blobs over the disk cap. The first over-cap run only warns and records a marker; run it again to evict. --dry-run prints what would go without touching anything; a plan reclaiming more than half the store is refused without --force. The sweep also runs automatically after every sync.
mp cutover [-A NAME] [--dry-run] End the pre-1.0 file-era layout: give any draft that has none an id: field, and report the old .md mailbox directories nothing reads any more

Mailypoppins used to keep received mail as one Markdown file per message under ~/.local/share/mailypoppins/accounts/<account>/. It now keeps it in a SQLite store beside a content-addressed blob store, and those old inbox/, archive/ and sent/ directories are dead weight. mp cutover is the one-time tidy-up: it lists each dead directory with its size and prints the rm line that removes it.

It never deletes anything itself, and there is no migration on startup: it runs only when you run it. Its one write is the id: frontmatter field, which is how a draft written by the old build becomes addressable by selector; running it again writes nothing, and --dry-run writes nothing at all. Drafts are the one thing whose truth is a local file (the server's Drafts folder holds a mirror of each, not the original), and they were never in the old directories to begin with.

Command Description
mp config init Interactive setup wizard
mp config show Display config (passwords masked)
mp config set-password Store a password in the active secrets backend (first account unless -A names one)
mp config reset-secrets Wipe the encrypted secrets file and Graph token caches, then re-prompt for credentials (after a restore to a new machine, or when the secrets file no longer decrypts)
mp config add-account Add a new account to the existing config
mp config oauth2-login Sign a Microsoft 365 (Graph) account in with the OAuth2 device code flow (first Graph account unless -A names one)
mp config path Print config file path

Daemon Commands

Command Description
mp daemon run [--foreground-logs] Run the daemon in the foreground; never connects to another daemon
mp daemon start [--timeout-secs N] Start the daemon (through the login service when one is installed for this data directory, detached otherwise) and return once it answers
mp daemon status [--json] Report whether a daemon is running against this data directory
mp daemon stop [--grace-secs N] [--timeout-secs N] Ask the running daemon to shut down, letting work in flight settle for the grace
mp daemon restart [--grace-secs N] Stop the running daemon and start this executable's, through the login service when one is installed, so a systemd unit or launchd agent stays in charge
mp daemon install-service [--check] [--force] Install the login-start service (systemd user unit or launchd agent) and enable it; --check reports and writes nothing
mp daemon uninstall-service Disable the login-start service and remove its file
mp daemon health [--json] Report the running daemon's health, its counters and its checks
mp daemon logs [--lines N] [--level LEVEL] [--json] Print the tail of the daemon's own structured log
mp daemon support-bundle [OUT] [--no-redact] Write a redacted support bundle and say what went into it
mp account list List the configured accounts, their backend and their state

Every command that touches your mail asks a background daemon over a Unix socket, and starts one if none is running. These manage it directly; mp daemon * never starts a daemon it was only asked to report on.

Shell Completions

mp completions <bash|zsh|fish|elvish|powershell> prints a completion script for every command and flag on stdout. It reads no config and needs no daemon. 

# zsh: save it on your fpath, then restart the shell
mp completions zsh > "${fpath[1]}/_mp"

# bash: load it in ~/.bashrc
eval "$(mp completions bash)"

Contacts Commands

Command Description
mp contacts search [<query>] [--parsable|--json] [-n N] Fuzzy-search the contact index by name and email; --parsable emits tab-delimited email/name lines for mutt, aerc or vim, --json one JSON object with the counts (default limit: 20)
mp contacts rebuild Rebuild the contact index from the local message store now (every account unless -A names one)
mp contacts stats Show contact index statistics

The contact index is a cache per account, contacts-cache.json in the account's data directory, ranked from the From, To, Cc and Bcc headers of the stored mail. Every sync and every send folds the mail it saw into it. The first search or stats of an account, from the CLI, the TUI or the desktop app, builds it before answering, and rebuilds it first when another version of mailypoppins built it, so a reinstall never keeps an index the current rules would not produce. mp contacts rebuild rebuilds it on demand.

Signature Commands

Command Description
mp signature list [--json] List the signatures, the account's default marked
mp signature show <name> [--path] Print a signature's content, or with --path the path of its file
mp signature new <name> Create an empty signature and print the path of its file
mp signature edit <name> Open a signature in $EDITOR
mp signature rename <old> <new> Rename a signature; an account default that named it follows
mp signature delete <name> Delete a signature, clearing any account default that named it
mp signature default [<name>|--none] Print the account's default signature, set it, or clear it with --none

A signature is one Markdown file under the configuration directory, and each account has its own default; -A names the account. The TUI's cs overlay and the Mac app's Signatures dialog manage the same files through the same daemon calls.

Sync Options

Command Description
-n, --limit <N> Max messages per mailbox (default: 50)
--mailbox <name>... Mailboxes to sync (default: INBOX, Archive, Sent)
--dry-run Show what would change without modifying files
--all-accounts Sync every configured account (names the failures, exits 1 if any failed)

Sync is additive by default: it fetches new emails only, deduplicated by Message-ID. A two-pass strategy first downloads headers (~50 bytes per message) to identify new emails, then fetches full RFC822 bodies only for messages not already stored locally.

Deletes are handled by the same pass. The download is capped by --limit, the enumeration never is, so a message the server no longer lists is pruned from the local store however far it sits below the newest ones, and a mailbox emptied elsewhere does not linger.

Invite Options (mp send --invite)

mp send --invite sends an iMIP calendar invitation (METHOD:REQUEST) over SMTP that renders as an actionable Accept / Tentative / Decline event in Outlook, Gmail, and Apple Mail. Attendees come from --to/--cc and the subject is reused as the event summary. Times accept local wall-clock (2026-07-20T14:00, "2026-07-20 14:00") or RFC3339 with an offset (2026-07-20T14:00:00+02:00, ...Z); a timed event needs either --end or --duration. The ORGANIZER is the sending account's primary address (Exchange drops mismatches). Graph accounts are not yet supported for invites.

A bare date as --start sends an all-day event, which calendars show in the all-day row. Without --end it covers that one day. --end names the last day, inclusive, so --start 2026-12-24 --end 2027-01-08 covers 24 December through 8 January; the invitation carries the day after as its exclusive DTEND, as RFC 5545 requires.

To change an invitation already sent, send it again with --uid set to its UID (shown in the preview and in its invite.ics) and a higher --sequence (the first send is 0, so the first update is 1). Calendar clients replace the event only when the UID matches and the sequence is higher than the one they hold; without --uid the invitation is a new event.

bash 
mp send --invite --to me@example.com --subject "Kita closed" --start 2026-12-24
mp send --invite --to me@example.com --subject "Christmas holidays" --start 2026-12-24 --end 2027-01-08
mp send --invite --to me@example.com --subject "Kita closed" --start 2026-12-24 \
  --uid 3f2a...@example.com --sequence 1
Command Description
--invite Send an iMIP calendar invitation (METHOD:REQUEST)
--to <addr> Attendee(s), comma-separated (also the To header)
--cc <addr> CC attendee(s), comma-separated
--subject <text> Event summary (reused as the email subject)
--start <when> Start: local time or RFC3339 with offset; a bare date (2026-12-24) makes an all-day event
--end <when> End, the same kind as --start; for an all-day event the last day, inclusive
--duration <dur> Duration instead of --end: PT1H30M or 1h30m; whole days (P3D, 3d) for an all-day event
--location <text> Optional event location
--description <text> Optional event description / body
--uid <uid> Re-send an invitation already sent, as an update of the event with this UID
--sequence <n> The update's SEQUENCE, higher than the last one sent for the UID (needs --uid)

Calendar Commands (mp calendar, mp event)

The calendar views merge two sources: the server calendar of an account whose calendar_backend is graph, which the daemon keeps a month back and a year ahead, and the invitation mails of every account, listed as its imip calendar. An invitation the server calendar also holds shows once, as the server's event. Each event line in a view carries your answer: ✓ accepted, ~ tentative, ✗ declined, ? not answered, ★ organizer. The event ids that mp event takes are in mp calendar view --json.

Command Description
mp calendar list [-A NAME] [--json] List the calendars with their account, name, id, backend, visibility and colour, the default one marked (every account unless -A names one)
mp calendar view [agenda|day|week] [--on DATE | --from DATE --to DATE] Show the events: the agenda from --on (default today) through 14 days later or from --from through --to, one day, or the ISO week holding --on. DATE is YYYY-MM-DD, today, tomorrow, yesterday or +N / -N days. -A NAME and --calendar ID (both repeatable) narrow the view, --hidden adds the hidden calendars, --zone reads the times in another IANA zone than the local one, and --json prints the calendar.view answer
mp calendar show|hide <calendar-id> [-A NAME] Show a hidden calendar in the views again, or hide one; a local preference that survives mp calendar rebuild
mp calendar freebusy [-A NAME] [--on DATE | --from DATE --to DATE] [ADDRESS]... Show when people and rooms are busy, your own row first: per address a row of 30-minute slots per day (· free, ▒ tentative, █ busy, ▓ away, ░ working elsewhere, ? unknown) and the busy blocks with their times; an address outside your organisation reads "no free/busy". --on is one day (default today), --from through --to up to 62 days, --interval MIN sets the slot length (5 to 1440), --zone ZONE the days' zone, --json prints the result. Needs a Microsoft 365 account
mp event create [-A NAME] --summary TEXT --start WHEN [--end WHEN | --duration D] Create an event in the account's server calendar, whose server sends the invitations: --to, --optional and --room invite people and rooms, --teams adds a Teams link on a calendar that offers Teams (one whose mailbox has no Teams licence refuses it), --reminder MIN or --no-reminder sets the reminder (the mailbox default otherwise), --location, --body or --body-file, --calendar ID (default the account's default calendar), --zone ZONE for the times (default the local zone); a bare date makes an all-day event whose --end is its last day; --transaction-id reruns a create with the id it printed when it could not confirm the event, so the server makes the event once; --json prints the result
mp event show <event-id> [-A NAME] [--json] Print one event: when, where, organizer, attendees with their answers and proposed times, your own answer, whether new times are accepted, the series rule (and whether this occurrence was changed), the online meeting and its service, link and description; --json adds the series of an occurrence
mp event respond <event-id> accept|tentative|decline [-A NAME] Answer an invitation through the server for a server event, or by iMIP reply for an invitation mail (imip:<row_id>); --comment TEXT adds a note, --no-send-response records the answer without telling the organizer (server events only), --json prints the result
mp invite accept|tentative|decline <selector> [--comment TEXT] [--no-send-response] Answer a received invitation mail: through the server when the account has a server calendar holding its event, else by iMIP REPLY
mp calendar reminders [-A NAME] [--json] List the reminders that fired and wait for you: the summary, when the event starts, where, and the account and event id a dismissal names (every account unless -A names one); --json prints the calendar.reminders answer
mp calendar reminder dismiss <event-id> [-A NAME] Dismiss an event's reminder in every client, and in Outlook on a Microsoft 365 account; a reminder dismissed before it fires does not fire
mp calendar reminder snooze <event-id> [--minutes N] [-A NAME] Snooze an event's reminder for N minutes (default 5) in every client, and in Outlook on a Microsoft 365 account
mp calendar rebuild [-A NAME] Report the attendee RSVPs resolved against your sent invites, and resync the server calendar of an account that has one (every account unless -A names one)
bash 
mp calendar view
mp calendar view week --on +7 -A evoqs
mp calendar hide AAMkADcal2 -A evoqs
mp calendar freebusy -A evoqs --on tomorrow ada@example.com room-1@example.com
mp event create -A evoqs --summary "Project review" --start 2026-11-18T14:00 --duration 1h --to ada@example.com --teams
mp event respond AAMkADev2 accept --comment "See you there" -A evoqs

In the TUI, the Calendar view (Space a) shows the same events of every account. a, d and w switch between the agenda, a day on an hour grid and the week in seven columns, which falls back to the day grid on a narrow terminal. h and l (or [ and ]) move by a day or a week, t goes back to today and gt jumps to a date. Enter opens the event card, V answers an invitation, n opens the event form on the cursor's day (Tab moves between its fields, Enter on the description opens $EDITOR, and Enter anywhere else creates the event), and c lists the calendars, where Space shows or hides one. A create that fails brings the form back as it was, and Enter retries it without making a second event. On a Microsoft 365 account the form shows the availability of you, the attendees and the rooms on the event's day, a row of 30-minute slots each from 07:00 to 20:00 with the chosen time marked, asked again half a second after you stop typing an address or the date; the desktop app's New event dialog shows the same as a coloured grid. A Graph account whose sign-in predates the calendar shows a banner over the view asking for mp config oauth2-login -A <name>, which leaves once the new sign-in lands.

Reminders (mp calendar reminders)

The daemon fires each server event's reminder at its due minute, the start minus the event's reminder setting in Outlook. A cancelled or declined event, one without a reminder and one in a hidden calendar never remind; a reminder that fell due while the daemon was stopped fires once when it starts, if its meeting has not ended. Only an account with a server calendar reminds, since an invitation mail carries no reminder setting of its own.

One client raises the system notification: the desktop app when it is open, else the TUI when notifications = true. Every open client shows the reminder in its own window, and a dismissal or a snooze in any of them clears or moves it in all of them. On a Microsoft 365 account the dismissal or the snooze reaches Outlook too, so your phone stops reminding of the same meeting; a meeting whose reminder you dismiss in Outlook leaves mp's list at the next sync.

bash 
mp calendar reminders
mp calendar reminder snooze AAMkADev2 --minutes 10 -A evoqs
mp calendar reminder dismiss AAMkADev2 -A evoqs

In the TUI the hint bar counts the waiting reminders, a reminder that fires shows on the status line, and R from any view lists them: s snoozes the one under the cursor for five minutes, d dismisses it and Enter opens its event in the Calendar view. In the desktop app a banner over the window lists them with Snooze and Dismiss, and a click on the notification brings the window forward on the event.

RSVP to Invitations (mp invite)

mp invite accept|tentative|decline <selector> answers a received calendar invitation mail. On an account whose server calendar holds the invitation's event, the answer goes through the server, as Outlook would send it, and --no-send-response records it without telling the organizer. Otherwise it reads the invite email's sidecar invite.ics (the source of truth for UID/SEQUENCE), builds a METHOD:REPLY with your account as the single ATTENDEE carrying the chosen PARTSTAT (ACCEPTED/TENTATIVE/DECLINED), and emails it to the ORGANIZER with an Outlook-convention subject (Accepted: <summary>, etc.). On a successful send the local event.rsvp is updated. --comment adds a note to either answer. v1 answers the whole series only (no per-occurrence responses).

In the TUI, invites show a calendar badge in the list and an event summary card at the top of the preview pane; press tv to open the respond overlay: Accept / Tentative / Decline, an optional comment, and, when the account's server calendar holds the event, whether to send the response. It answers the way mp invite does. An iMIP reply is emailed to the organizer only: it does not reach a server calendar. A Graph account answers only through its server calendar, so it needs calendar_backend = "graph".

A reply sent from a Proton account is not recorded by Exchange and Microsoft 365 organizers, because Proton turns its calendar part into an attachment on the way out. Answer such an invitation from another account or from Proton's own client.

Organizer RSVP Tracking (mp calendar rebuild)

When someone accepts or declines an invitation you sent with mp send --invite, their reply arrives as a METHOD:REPLY email during normal sync. mailypoppins matches it by event UID to your sent invitation and shows that attendee's status on the invite, so you can see who responded. The statuses are computed from the stored invitation and reply messages every time they are shown, so the agenda and the preview card are always current with what has arrived.

mp calendar rebuild [-A NAME] reports what those replies resolve across every stored invitation (defaults to all accounts). It writes nothing: there is no cached copy of the statuses to rebuild, so it is idempotent by construction, and two machines syncing the same account see identical state with no direct machine-to-machine sync. Replies for a SEQUENCE older than the invitation's are ignored, and the most recent reply per attendee wins. Nothing is written back to the server. On an account with a server calendar it also drops the daemon's copy of that calendar and reads it afresh, keeping which calendars are hidden, and reports the calendars and events it read.

Global Options

Command Description
-A, --account <name> Account to use, before or after the command (default: first in config; mp calendar rebuild, mp calendar list, mp calendar view, mp calendar reminders, mp cutover and mp contacts rebuild cover every account unless it names one, and mp calendar view takes it more than once; mp -A <name> with no command opens the TUI on that account). Refused by the commands that act on no account: mp daemon, mp completions, mp dump-keys, mp account list, and mp config init, show, add-account, reset-secrets and path

Signature Options

The commands that write a signature into a draft, and mp send --invite, whose invitation carries one, take these two after the command name.

Command Description
-s, --signature <name> Use a specific signature (mp new, mp reply, mp forward, and mp send --invite)
--no-signature Skip signature entirely (the same four)

Search Query Syntax

The mp search command, its --local mode and the TUI server search overlay (f) all speak one grammar. Fields AND together, (a OR b) groups an alternation, and quoted values are supported (e.g., from:"John Doe"). Sylvain's example from:boss@corp.com (invoice OR receipt) has:attachment runs on every backend. Without an in: prefix or --mailbox, all the account's mailboxes are searched, and on Exchange every folder, each hit listed under the folder it sits in. A malformed query is an error with a caret pointing at the problem, never a silent search for less.

The daemon runs every server search, and mp search, the TUI overlay and the desktop app's search bar make the same call. A mailbox the server refuses does not stop the others: mp search prints Search in <mailbox> failed on stderr after the results, and the same line names any hit the server matched but did not hand over. When more matched than are shown, mp search ends with More results than the 20 shown: raise -n to see them., and the TUI and the desktop app end their count with the same sentence and a narrower search as the remedy.

Command Description
from: Filter by sender
to: Filter by recipient
cc: Filter by CC
subject: Filter by subject
body: Filter by body content
filename: Match an attachment filename (Gmail/Exchange/--local only)
has:attachment Only mail carrying an attachment
after: On or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD (since: is an alias)
before: Strictly before this date, YYYY-MM-DD
message-id: Exact RFC 5322 Message-ID lookup; angle brackets optional
in: Restrict search to a mailbox
"a phrase" A quoted phrase is one term
(a OR b) An OR group; AND-ed with the rest of the query
bare text Matches any field

Flags (same query, for scripting)

Every field has a matching flag; a flag invocation builds the identical query as its positional twin, so mp search --from boss@corp.com --has-attachment 'invoice OR receipt' equals mp search 'from:boss@corp.com (invoice OR receipt) has:attachment'.

Command Description
--from / --to / --cc / --subject / --body / --filename <s> The field prefixes as flags; they build the same query
--has-attachment Only mail carrying an attachment (has:attachment)
--after / --before <YYYY-MM-DD> The date range as flags
--mailbox <name> Scope to one mailbox by role, label or server name: any folder the server lists (--local: any mailbox of the sidebar)
-n, --limit <N> Max results across every searched mailbox, newest first (default: 20): each mailbox is asked for its newest N, and only the N newest overall are downloaded; a server search cut by it ends with a "raise -n" line; Exchange stops a search at 1000 results per mailbox, so a larger limit there says to narrow the query instead
--full Show full body instead of preview
--local Search the local FTS index offline instead of the server
--json Print the hits as one JSON object on stdout, with "truncated": true when more matched than --limit let through; warnings stay on stderr

has:attachment across backends

On Gmail and Microsoft Exchange has:attachment runs server-side. Plain IMAP (RFC 3501) has no attachment search key, so mp answers that part from the local store's synced mail and prints a warning that un-synced mail is not covered; run mp sync for full coverage. The result header on stdout repeats it, as in Fetched Emails (3 results, local store only: has:attachment) or No results found (local store only: has:attachment), so a script that drops stderr still sees it, and --json carries "coverage": "local" with the term in local_terms ("coverage": "server" when the server answered every term). The TUI's server search overlay and the desktop app's search bar put the same caveat after their count, as in 2 results (local store only: has:attachment).

Local full-text search (--local)

mp search --local <query> answers from the local store's FTS5 index instead of the server: offline, ranked best match first, and covering every synced mailbox of the account at once. A subject hit outranks the same word buried in a quoted reply. The index is written in the same transaction as the message it describes, so it is never stale with respect to what mp sync has pulled, and it holds only what has been synced, which is what the server-side search is still for. Punctuation is searched as text, not as query syntax.

Command Description
word Matches the whole word in subject, sender or body; several words all have to match
"a phrase" Matches the words adjacent, in that order
word* Prefix match (invoi* finds invoicing)
subject: Restrict the term to the subject
from: Restrict the term to the sender
body: Restrict the term to the body text
--mailbox <name> Restrict the search to one mailbox (default: the whole account)

TUI Key Bindings

Generated from the single KEYMAP source of truth (clients/tui/src/app/keymap.rs) via mp dump-keys --json; see scripts/regen-website-keys.sh. These match the in-TUI help overlay (?) exactly.

The copy keys (y, and c in Contacts) write to the system clipboard. Over ssh the remote host usually has none, so the TUI sends the text to your terminal as an OSC 52 escape sequence instead. Ghostty, WezTerm, kitty, iTerm2 and tmux with set-clipboard on put it on your local clipboard. The status line then shows the copied text, so you can still select it by hand in a terminal that ignores OSC 52.
